newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher on moderate volumes.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher on moderate volumes.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended lower Monday, after opening steady and then drifting lower, on moderate estimated total volume of 9,000 lots.

"The funds have been near their limits on long positions and the market has been overbought after reaching eight month highs earlier this month, so we are seeing some fund liquidation, but support is still holding," one trader said.
In the latest CFTC Commitments of Traders data released late Friday, funds and small traders remain heavily net long COMEX copper at a level little changed from two weeks ago.
"Copper looks like its heading into a range until after the Easter holiday," he said.
COMEX May copper ended down 1.85 cent at 110.75 cents a pound, after trading a 111.90-109.50 range.
The COMEX May/July backwardation ended little changed around 3.20 cents a pound, while the LME cash-to-three month spread firmed to $73.00 a tonne from last week's lows below $50.00.
But steady U.S. economic growth, Japanese buying for preferential tariff purchases, and the potential for Chinese buying are keeping the market firm, analysts said.

But Far East metals traders were bearish Monday about China's short term role in the world copper market, even though an offical of the China Nonferrous Metals Import and Export Corp (CNIEC) said no directives had been issued to suspend copper imports.
